newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends down in line with Japan.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends down in line with Japan.

text.p: Rubber futures finished lower on Tuesday in line with falls in Japanese prices although buying picked up as people engaged in brisk shortcovering, dealers said.
"There was pretty good shortcovering for RSS3 grade rubber and the good mood spread at least to TSR20 rubber," a trader for a foreign brokerage house said.
"The prices here were seen to go lower due to the lower prices in Japan," another trader said.
Tokyo's benchmark August contract shed 2.3 yen to finish at 153.7 yen.

The volume traded for RSS3 rubber reached nearly 8,600 tonnes, slightly topping the 8,510 tonnes traded yesterday. The total traded for TSR20 rubber rose to around 6,200 tonnes, up sharply from the 600 tonnes total on Monday.
At around 0945 GMT, May RSS3 was seen at 121.00-123.00 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 123.25 cents.

May RSS1 was indicated at 172.50-174.50 Singapore cents (US$1.20-$1.22) a kg from 175.75 cents. May TSR20 was seen at 162.50-164.50 Singapore cents (US$1.13-$1.15) a kg from the previous 166.50 cents.
